notes: Stage A is None: a walkable named ship is a place, not a game type, so no-genre.md was loaded and no genre was invented for it.

Verticality overrides the Explorable Place preset's all-defaults shape. A liner's boat deck overhangs the promenade below it, so the overhang cost is inherent to the subject even though the user never mentioned decks or levels. That is where P2 comes from.
75 lifeboats is a spatial constraint, not dressing. At roughly 10 studs of davit each, about 37 per side needs 400+ studs of side deck, which is what pushed the scale band up to district.
Nothing in the emit schema carries a count, so '75' and 'two masts' survive only inside free text.
'a two Red Funnel ship' was read as two red funnels. Red Funnel is also a real ferry line, so that reading is an assumption.

notes: First-person camera, WASD movement, the HUD countdown, the game-over state and the restart are all mechanics and UI. The only thing the timer does to the layout is bound its size: the maze has to be crossable inside the countdown at 16 studs per second.

P6 comes from the maze shape, which is exactly the right route here: the topology is generated procedurally so a reachable exit is guaranteed, then dressed. A free image of a maze can produce one with no exit at all.
Puzzle has no start-point option and no win-volume option, so both are id:null layout picks even though this prompt is explicit about each.
trigger-solve was not taken separately; the keyhole is folded into the exit gate rather than placed as its own receptacle.
The user forbade clarifying questions. Theme is genuinely unstated, so it is emitted null and the next step should use neutral dressing rather than invent a look.

open_questions.ask: What is the maze made of: concrete, hedge, dungeon stone, sci-fi panels? Emitted null because you asked for no questions.
How many seconds on the clock? At 16 studs per second that number is the maximum solvable maze size.

notes: Adventure is dominant because gathering every crystal across an open terrain is a scavenger hunt. Puzzle was loaded as a secondary purely for the button and gate options, which Adventure genuinely cannot express, and only options were taken from it.
Preset option alcove-secret was dropped: the prompt says the crystals lie in the open literally everywhere, which is the opposite of hidden discovery alcoves.
P2 comes from the moving bridges, which span gaps and so overhang the ground below. The terrain's own hills and valleys are tiered, not overhanging, and would be P0 + tiered on their own.

CHECK the crystal density against the band. At district scale, one crystal every metre in every direction is on the order of hundreds of thousands of instances. Either the map is much smaller than assumed or 'every metre' is a figure of speech, and this should be resolved before a build runs.

The buttons change world state: the same door locks and unlocks, the same lava turns off and on. Every option in the loaded files describes one static placement, so the map's second configuration is not represented anywhere in this handoff.
'Objects on top of' the terrain was left unspecified and nothing was built for it.

gaps.genre_gap: Adventure took this because 'gather all the crystals' is a scavenger hunt, but nothing here is story or exploration driven. It is a hazard-and-switch sandbox, and the fit is partly forced: world-open is the right shape, but the Adventure options around it (quest boards, discovery alcoves, story locks, cinematic reveals) describe a different kind of game, and the two picks that carry the prompt's actual character both came from a secondary genre file.

Every option in every loaded file describes one static placement, so a map whose lava, bridges and doors change state on a button press can only be expressed as the first of its two configurations plus a note. There is no way to say 'this door has an open state and a closed state and both must be traversable geometry'.
